title: Remote corpus daemon cannot render project provider files or read repo-owned knowledge
wanted_capability: bbox_render scope=project (and repo-owned .bbox/knowledge reads/writes) against a checkout that lives on a satellite machine, when blackboxd runs as the remote corpus host (cage). The remote daemon has no filesystem access to the checkout: real render fails with ENOENT and dry-run silently shows a central-store-only view that would clobber the 71 repo-owned entries down to 1 if written. Needs a satellite-side render path (collector/fleetd-mediated, or a bbox CLI render against the local checkout) or an explicit fail-closed guard naming the limitation. Same limitation recursively: bbox_gap and bbox_learn project-scoped writes land in the remote daemon's state instead of the repo-owned .bbox/ stores (this file is a hand-mirror of the daemon-side gap record).
evidence: bbox_render project ENOENT + dry-run showing 1 entry vs 71 repo-owned (2026-07-18)
local 7264 closed; corpus role served from the cage deployment
.bbox/knowledge/891f4a74.json + AGENTS.md block hand-materialized as the workaround
notes: Filed via the remote daemon (record exists in its store under the same dedupe_key); mirrored here so the repo-owned gap store stays authoritative per the repo-owned-project-state convention.
resolution_note: Shipped in ac55feae91a8: corpus-role render guard + pending-placement notices, GET /render/plan + POST /render/ack, and `bro render` satellite apply (byte-identical splices, generated-header gate, >50% shrink guard, repo-record drain + ack). Proven live against the cage; residual cross-host identity mismatch tracked as gap-cbcc314d.
